body:
## Pull request overview

This PR updates the Service AI agent chat endpoint to accept Vercel AI SDK v6 message payloads that provide `parts` arrays instead of `content` strings, aligning the agent route behavior with the existing general chat route. It centralizes message normalization/validation into a shared utility to keep route behavior consistent.

**Changes:**
- Add shared `normalizeMessage()` + `validateMessageContent()` utilities and reuse them from both `ai-routes` and `agent-routes`.
- Update agent chat request validation to accept `parts`-based messages and normalize messages before invoking `chatWithTools()`.
- Add agent-route tests for v6 `parts` scenarios and document the fix in the changelog.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/message-utils.ts | New shared message normalization + content/parts validation helpers. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/index.ts | Re-export shared message utilities from the routes entrypoint. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/ai-routes.ts | Replace inlined normalization/validation with shared helpers. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/agent-routes.ts | Accept v6 `parts` messages; normalize messages before calling `chatWithTools()`. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/__tests__/chatbot-features.test.ts | Add coverage for agent endpoint handling of `parts` format messages. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Note the agent chat v6 `parts` support under Unreleased fixes. |
</details>

`validateMessageContent()` currently treats the mere presence of a `parts` array as valid (no element/shape checks). This allows inputs like `parts: [null]` (which can crash `normalizeMessage`) or `parts: []` / non-text-only parts that normalize to an empty prompt. Suggest validating `parts` elements similarly to `content[]` (non-null objects with string `type`, and `text` when type is `text`), and (optionally) requiring at least one usable text part when `allowEmptyContent` is false.
